description: Multi-tap delay whose taps are tapped in by hand: each tap on the sensor adds another echo at the time you tapped it

params.text: Sets the level of the input going into the delay
Scales the whole tap pattern in time, stretching or shrinking every tap together
Sets how much of the delayed signal is fed back in
Sets how much the tap times wander under their own slow random modulation
Crossfades the output between the dry input and the taps
Sets how long the module takes to fade from one tap pattern to the next
A short press loads the pattern held in that slot of the current bank; holding it offers to save the pattern into that slot, which a second press on the same button confirms
Chooses what tapping does: OFF adds no taps at all, ADD builds a pattern from the taps as they come, and INS folds each new tap into the length of the pattern already there
A short press turns repeat on and off, which loops the tap pattern; a long press clears every tap
Tap it to add a tap at that moment; the first tap starts the count and the ones after it set the times
A short press removes the last tap added; a long press turns tap quantising on and off
Chooses what a tap's velocity changes: AMP its level, LPF a low-pass filter on it, and RES a band-pass filter on it

inputs.text: Moves the TIME knob; the voltage is read upside down, so -5V stretches the pattern and +5V shrinks it
Moves the FEEDBACK knob; the voltage is read upside down, so -5V raises it and +5V lowers it
Moves the MODULATION knob; the voltage is read upside down, so -5V raises it and +5V lowers it
Moves the DRY/WET knob; the voltage is read upside down, so -5V goes wetter and +5V drier
The signal to be delayed, up to 22V
A gate above 0.5V turns repeat on and off
A rising edge above 0.5V adds a tap at that moment, in place of tapping the sensor
Sets the velocity given to the next tap added, 0V to 8V
A clock above 0.5V that new taps are quantised to

outputs.text: An 8V pulse, 4ms long, each time a tap is detected
The left side of the delay, or both sides summed when OUT 2 is empty
The right side of the delay

notes: The module does nothing until taps are entered: tap the sensor, or send edges to the TAP jack, and each one after the first adds an echo.
With nothing patched into AUDIO OUT 2, AUDIO OUT 1 carries both sides summed; patching OUT 2 splits them.
menu: Velocity: Min, Low, Med, High, Max — sets the velocity a new tap is given when nothing is patched into the velocity jack
Bank: A, B, C, D — chooses which bank of six saved patterns the six buttons reach
Pan: SUM/R, RND, ALT — sets where each new tap is placed across the two outputs: all to one side, at random, or alternating
Mode: Edit, Seq — chooses whether the taps work as a delay being edited or as a sequence

inputs.5: high above 0.5V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.6: high above 0.5V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.7:
0 to 8V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.8: high above 0.5V · stepped · one channel only
